newsitem.title: PERU: Bullish mining stocks push Lima mkt to higher end.
newsitem.headline: Bullish mining stocks push Lima mkt to higher end.

text.p: Mining stocks set the pace on Tuesday, pushing the Lima Stock Exchange index to close one percent higher, but traders expected investors to start taking profits Wednesday after recent record bull runs in the sector.
Brokers added market interest in miners would continue as the economic climate for the sector in Peru remained favorable and international zinc price looked firm.

The blue-chip index closed up 1.09 percent at 2,703.70 points, while the general index climbed up 0.95 percent to 1,854.10 points, according to preliminary figures at the market's 1330 local time (1830 GMT) close.
"The forecast for zinc price are very attractive. Zinc tonnage is estimated to reach $1,600 by the end of the year," said trader Manuel Torres at brokerage Finvest.
Most investor attention was on mining company Atacocha, which closed up 8.93 percent at 1.83 soles, with 1.7 million shares traded.

"Regarding Atacocha the rumors are that sales have tripled in April and that investors are betting on the financial results in June," Torres said. Its share price has risen 46 percent so far this month, also helped by miner's cost-cutting program to reduce its workforce.
Mining firm Morococha also saw bullish trade, closing up 8.06 percent at 4.02 soles, with 429,480 shares changing hands.
"In the case of Morococha what's still influencing it is the Phelps Dodge Corp purchase," added Torres. Morococha announced last week that Phelps Dodge had bought a 27 percent stake in the firm.
Elsewhere Peru's largest cement maker Cementos Lima closed up 5.41 percent at 5.07 soles, while blue- chip heavyweight Telefonica del Peru lost ground to close down 0.3 percent at 6.60 soles.
